newsitem.title: USA: Smith Barney to spend $250 mln on NextGen.
newsitem.headline: Smith Barney to spend $250 mln on NextGen.

text.p: Smith Barney will likely spend $250-$300 million for its new NextGen brokerage technology, Smith Barney chief executive Jamie Dimon said.

Smith Barney expects to complete installing about 20,000 broker computer workstations and 500 servers by the end of next year, and has already begun the rollout, according to Jay Mandelbaum, director of retail marketing and client services.

NextGen will permit a broker -- called a financial consultant by Smith Barney -- to get market data and news, and immediate and detailed information on client accounts, as well as the current value of their portfolios.
The executives spoke at a press briefing to unveil NextGen and its new Internet interactive web site, called Access.
Steve Clifford, Smith Barney Internet product manager, said its new web site would be unveiled next month.

In a demonstration to reporters, Smith Barney executives showed how customers would be able to get quick access to their accounts and receive immediate data on the value of their holdings, including stock, bond, and mutual funds.
The site would give stock prices, with a 20-minute delay. Customers could also send electronic messages to their brokers.
Clifford said that Smith Barney would permit individuals who were not clients to sample the service for a few months, then they would be encouraged to open an account.
In his presentation, Dimon said he expected the NextGen technology to be cheaper than similar technology at financial services competitors, such as Merrill Lynch and Co Inc.
Merrill said it was unfair to compare the cost of the two system. In May, Merrill announced the launch of its Trusted Global Advisor system at a cost of about $800 million.

Merrill said its system included at least $200 million for a communications network and a five-year operating service agreement for market data and telecommunications. Also included are 25,000 desktop personal computers, 1,200 branch servers and 8,000 printers.
Smith Barney is a unit of Travelers Group Inc.
